postings: ANM at Sub-Centre / Ayushman Arogya Mandir (outreach)
ANM.summary: The ANM is the first-level skilled health worker for a sub-centre population of about 5,000. She delivers antenatal, postnatal and newborn care, immunisation and family planning services at the sub-centre and in outreach sessions. She screens adults for common non-communicable diseases and follows up communicable disease cases under national programmes. She supervises and supports ASHAs and works with the Anganwadi Worker and the Village Health Sanitation and Nutrition Committee. At a delivery-point PHC she also assists with normal deliveries and immediate newborn care. She maintains the RCH and programme registers and enters data on the RCH portal and U-WIN. She refers complications to the PHC or FRU using the referral protocols. In {state} she works within the state's programme priorities listed under state context.
authorised: Register pregnant women and provide antenatal check-ups, including blood pressure, haemoglobin and urine tests
Give Td, and vaccines under the Universal Immunisation Programme
Conduct normal deliveries at a designated delivery point and give immediate newborn care
Provide oral contraceptive pills, condoms and emergency contraception; insert IUCD where trained
Screen adults for hypertension, diabetes and common cancers using programme tools
Treat minor ailments with drugs on the sub-centre list
notAuthorised: Manage eclampsia, obstructed labour or postpartum haemorrhage beyond first aid: stabilise and refer
Prescribe drugs outside the sub-centre essential medicines list
Perform MTP procedures: counsel and refer under the MTP (Amendment) Act 2021
stateContext: Follow {state}'s programme priorities and IEC languages
Use the state's name for the sub-centre cadre where it differs
Note endemic diseases relevant to {state} (vector-borne disease, TB burden) for NCVBDC and NTEP follow-up
assumptions: Sub-centre population of about 5,000 (3,000 in hilly and tribal areas)
verify: Current state notification of delivery points for ANMs
Whether IUCD insertion is part of the state's ANM job description

roles.title: Conduct antenatal care at the sub-centre and in outreach
activities: Register pregnant women within 12 weeks and issue the MCP card
Measure blood pressure, weight and haemoglobin at each antenatal visit
Test urine for protein and sugar
Identify high-risk pregnancies and refer to the PHC
Give Td doses and iron-folic acid tablets as per schedule
Counsel on birth preparedness and danger signs
Follow up women who miss antenatal visits

roles.title: Conduct Village Health Sanitation and Nutrition Days (VHSND)
activities: Plan the VHSND session with the AWW and ASHA
Set up the session site with privacy and equipment
Provide antenatal, immunisation and growth monitoring services at the session
Conduct group counselling on nutrition and sanitation
Record services given in the VHSND register
Line-list beneficiaries who did not attend for follow-up
Report session outcomes to the PHC

roles.title: Provide immunisation services
activities: Prepare the due list for each session from U-WIN
Maintain the cold chain during transport and the session
Administer vaccines with correct dose, route and site
Observe children for 30 minutes after vaccination
Dispose of sharps and vials as per biomedical waste rules
Update U-WIN records the same day

roles.title: Support safe delivery and immediate newborn care
activities: Monitor labour using the WHO Labour Care Guide
Conduct a normal delivery with active management of the third stage
Resuscitate a newborn who does not breathe at birth
Identify maternal and newborn complications and refer
Prepare the labour room as per LaQshya checklists

roles.title: Provide postnatal and home-based newborn care
activities: Examine the mother within 48 hours of delivery
Check the newborn for danger signs on scheduled home visits
Counsel on exclusive breastfeeding and thermal care
Identify low birth weight babies and plan extra visits
Refer sick newborns to the SNCU or NBSU
Record postnatal visits on the RCH portal

roles.title: Provide family planning counselling and services
activities: Counsel couples on the full basket of contraceptive choices
Provide oral pills, condoms and emergency contraception
Insert and remove IUCD where trained
Follow up clients for side effects

roles.title: Screen and follow up non-communicable diseases
activities: Screen adults over 30 for hypertension and diabetes
Conduct oral, breast and cervical cancer screening as per training
Refer screen-positive clients to the PHC medical officer
Dispense monthly medicines to confirmed patients as prescribed
Counsel on diet, physical activity and tobacco cessation
Track treatment adherence in the NCD register
Enter screening data in the NCD portal

roles.title: Manage communicable disease surveillance and follow-up
activities: Report fever and diarrhoea cases on the S form
Collect blood slides or RDTs for suspected malaria
Identify presumptive TB cases and refer for testing
Support treatment adherence for TB patients under NTEP
Investigate clusters of cases with the PHC team
Conduct contact tracing for notifiable diseases
Educate families on prevention of vector-borne diseases

roles.title: Promote child nutrition and growth monitoring
activities: Weigh and measure children under five
Plot growth on the MCP card
Identify children with severe acute malnutrition and refer
Distribute vitamin A and deworming tablets as per schedule
Coordinate with the AWW on supplementary nutrition
Follow up children discharged from NRC

roles.title: Maintain records, registers and RCH portal entries
activities: Maintain the sub-centre registers as prescribed
Enter beneficiary data on the RCH portal
Prepare the monthly service delivery report
Correct data errors flagged by the block
Present sub-centre data at monthly meetings

roles.title: Manage drugs, vaccines and supplies
activities: Indent drugs and consumables every month
Check expiry dates and remove expired stock
Report stock-outs to the PHC pharmacist
Account for supplies used in outreach

roles.title: Supervise and support ASHAs
activities: Hold monthly review meetings with ASHAs
Identify ASHA training needs and report them

roles.title: Mobilise the community and coordinate with local bodies
activities: Attend Village Health Sanitation and Nutrition Committee meetings
Present local health data to the Panchayat
Plan health camps with the community
Engage community leaders to address vaccine hesitancy
Coordinate with the AWW on joint activities

roles.title: Respond to emergencies and refer appropriately
activities: Recognise danger signs in mothers, newborns and children
Give first aid and stabilise before referral
Arrange transport through the ambulance service
Fill the referral slip with key findings
Follow up referred patients after discharge
Report maternal and infant deaths for review
